blocks.text: Mount a named volume at the data directory the image actually uses, and remember that POSTGRES_* variables apply only on first initialization.

blocks.code:
services:
  db:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg17
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_DB: rag
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/db_password
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    shm_size: 256mb
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:5432:5432"]
volumes:
  pgdata:

rows: Wrong mount path → data lands in an anonymous volume
Up to PG17: /var/lib/postgresql/data; postgres:18 images moved to a versioned layout under /var/lib/postgresql, so check the image docs
Major upgrade on the same volume fails ("incompatible")
pg_dump/pg_restore into a new volume, or pg_upgrade
Mounting a filesystem root with lost+found

blocks.text: $ docker compose exec db psql -U app -d rag -c "SHOW data_directory;"
Changing POSTGRES_PASSWORD on an existing volume does nothing to the stored password; the app then fails authentication.

Q: "How do you persist Postgres in Docker safely?" A: "A named volume at the image's real data directory, credentials applied once at init (change them later with ALTER USER), enough shm_size, the port bound to loopback or unpublished, and major upgrades via dump/restore into a new volume."

items: Named volume at the correct PGDATA path.
POSTGRES_* only apply on first init.
